messages:

Subject: Fwd: Finex DPA — quick alignment before we send redlines

Monica / Evelyn — I had the discovery call this morning with Finex. They are on a tight timeline to close next-week and need two things clarified before legal will approve: (1) subprocessors list for Private (VPC) option and (2) a short clause on offline incident notification for on-prem customers.

I attached the draft DPA they shared (their template) and a checklist of the ask. Can you review the two redlines I highlighted and confirm whether we can accept the on-prem SLA language they require?

Quick notes:
- Finex is a healthtech customer (PHI decision pending), they prefer Private/VPC but may consider Dedicated with strict contractual isolation.
- Procurement wants DocuSign by Friday.

Thanks — I can hop on a short call if easier.

—Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Finex DPA — quick alignment before we send redlines

Thanks Karthik — I reviewed Finex's template and drafted targeted redlines. High-level:
1) Subprocessors: we can provide the full list for the Hosted/Dedicated stacks, but for Private/VPC/on-prem we need to avoid naming certain infra partners that customers manage directly. Proposed compromise: add a clause that Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors used for support/maintenance activities that will have access to telemetry and logs, and commit to 30 days notice for additions. For on-prem, limit our subprocessors to remote-support tooling only.

2) Data transfer clause: Finex wants an EU/UK standard clause; they are US-based but have EU presence. We should offer Standard Contractual Clauses for any cross-border transfers and a supplemental addendum for the on-prem mode that clarifies no cross-border copying without customer's consent.

3) Incident notification: Their ask to notify "within 24 hours" for any suspected data access is aggressive. Recommend 72 hours for confirmed breaches and 24 hours for high-risk exfiltration events — we'll map severity levels in the annex.

I attached a redline of their DPA (Redwood_DPA_Private_v2_redline.docx). If you approve, I'll send to Finex legal with a short cover note and the subprocessors CSV.

—Monica

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Private_v2_redline.docx (docx)

From: Asha Rao <asha@finexhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Murray <tom.murray@finexhealth.com>, legal-ops@finexhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finex DPA — Redwood redlines received

Hi Karthik / Monica — thank you for the quick turnaround and the redline. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Subprocessors disclosure: we need the full list that could have access to telemetry/logs for support (we will treat it under our internal whitelisting process). The CSV looks fine but can you confirm whether any subcontractors are used for support escalation (e.g., remote-run partners)?
- On-prem clause: our security team requires a statement that Redwood will not transfer customer data outside the customer's VPC or on-prem environment for any purpose other than explicit maintenance activities and only with explicit written consent for transfers.
- Incident windows: 24 hours for suspected access is our baseline for regulated data — we can be flexible on confirmed/severity tiering as long as suspected access gets immediate notification.

We can accept 72 hours for confirmed incidents if you provide a faster path to escalate high-severity events (e.g., dedicated pager + direct phone).

Can you share a DocuSign link once we align on the final language? Procurement wants the signature flow tracked.

—Asha

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@finexhealth.com>, Tom Murray <tom.murray@finexhealth.com>, legal-ops@finexhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Finex DPA — Redwood redlines received

Hi Asha / Tom — appreciate the thoughtful feedback. We've made three targeted updates in the attached redline to reflect your asks:
1) Subprocessors: attached CSV is expanded to include escalation partners; for Private/VPC we explicitly list only support tooling vendors (remote debug/telemetry) and state that any additional subprocessor access requires written customer approval.
2) On-prem transfers: added a clause — "Redwood will not transfer or copy Customer Data outside the Customer-controlled environment except as necessary for maintenance with prior written consent; any cross-border transfer requires Customer authorization."
3) Incident notification: we accepted a hybrid approach — immediate notification for suspected high-risk exposures (we included criteria), 72-hour window for confirmed breaches, and an escalation path including a 24x7 incident phone and a dedicated Slack channel.

I have attached the updated redline (Redwood_DPA_Private_v2_redline.docx) and the subprocessors CSV. If this looks good, Karthik will drop the DocuSign envelope.

—Monica
